text:
ConocoPhillips recovered 0.84% today, climbing back to $136.12 after hitting $134.40 yesterday—the low point of a sharp four-day slide from $142.28 last Thursday. The bounce likely reflects the geopolitical tensions in the Middle East: reports of Iranian and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia and Bahrain over the past day can tighten oil markets on supply-disruption fears, and WTI crude sitting near $90 per barrel provides a floor that supports energy stocks even after recent weakness.

The stock has surrendered ground as a broader energy sell-off, but the news today about rising electricity demand from data centers and potential European gas shortages from depleted winter storage could underpin longer-term demand for energy supplies—though today's small recovery suggests investors remain cautious about near-term direction.
